paper.title_en: An ML-based hybrid task scheduler for classical-quantum computing environments using real graph-derived workloads
paper.abstract_en: We evaluate learned placement between a central processing unit and a simulated-quantum processing unit using 2400 optimization tasks from 1,200 region-separated network subgraphs. Training-fitted service and quality predictors prevent post-execution feature leakage. Random Forest achieves external accuracy 0.956111 and simulated-quantum F1 0.935352, with region-bootstrap intervals of 0.949722-0.963611 and 0.923661-0.947530. Nine policies are compared under five synthetic traffic scenarios using thirty paired replay seeds and measured inference overhead. Under busy classical resources, learned routing reduces mean response from 0.171080 to 0.117594 s relative to classical-only execution, but direct objective routing and a threshold heuristic are faster. Ablations and holdouts expose dependence on queue state and weaknesses under size shifts. Calibration selects zero quantum angles, making the simulated path uniform sampling with classical decoding. The results support controlled scheduling evaluation, while physical quantum advantage and deployment readiness remain unestablished.
